Bayesian journey to crime

Source: R/sp.R
bjtc.Rd

Combines a journey-to-crime surface over origin zones with an origin-destination matrix of solved offences (Levine 2009; Levine and Block 2011): P(Jtc), the surface; P(O), the origins of all solved offences; P(O|Jtc), the origins of offences in the zones where the series happened; their product, Bayes' numerator with the surface as prior; and the risk, the product over P(O), renormalised. Each block sums to 1. The matrix describes past solved offences and inherits their selection.

Usage

bjtc(pj, od, dest)

Arguments

pj

The journey-to-crime value of each origin zone: numbers from 0, not all 0.

od

The origin-destination counts: a matrix with one row per origin zone and one column per destination zone, numbers from 0.

dest

The destination zone (column of od) of each incident of the series: whole numbers from 1; repeats count.

Value

A data frame with one row per origin zone: pj, po, pod, prod and risk (0 where po is 0).

References

Levine, N. and Block, R. (2011). Bayesian journey-to-crime estimation: an improvement in geographic profiling methodology. The Professional Geographer, 63(2), 213-229. doi:10.1080/00330124.2010.547152

Examples

od <- matrix(c(5, 1, 0, 2, 4, 1, 0, 1, 6), 3)
bjtc(pj = c(0.5, 0.3, 0.2), od = od, dest = c(1, 2, 2))
#>    pj   po  pod       prod       risk
#> 1 0.5 0.35 0.45 0.59210526 0.55900621
#> 2 0.3 0.30 0.45 0.35526316 0.39130435
#> 3 0.2 0.35 0.10 0.05263158 0.04968944
